answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The nebula multiplier is published, charged in gale, and hollow lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4040 identities would post 2570 proofs and burn roughly 77 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
